title: Webb Telescope Finds a Giant Galaxy Group That Grew Too Fast
summary:
NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has studied a huge group of galaxies called XLSSC 122. It is about 10.4 billion light-years away. That means we see it as it looked about 10 billion years ago.

A group like this is called a galaxy cluster. Even long ago, XLSSC 122 already looked big and organized. A lot of its mass is packed tightly in the middle. Scientists' models say clusters should have grown more slowly, so this one is a puzzle.

The cluster's strong gravity bends light from galaxies behind it. This is called strong gravitational lensing. XLSSC 122 is now the most distant cluster known to do this.

The bent light helps scientists measure dark matter. Dark matter is invisible, but its gravity pulls on everything around it. Scientist Kyle Finner said lensing lets them measure dark matter without actually seeing it.
why_it_matters: Looking far into space helps kids and scientists learn how the universe, and everything in it, came to be.
